verdict.rationale: Bruno's own docs say collections are saved to a folder on your filesystem as plain-text Bru markup, and that you can version them with Git and review changes like code. Git collaboration works through both the terminal (git init in the collection directory) and a built-in Git UI. A community comment independently describes the plain-text, commit-to-repo design as Bruno's main benefit. Missing for 10: hands-on independent evidence of diff/merge behavior on .bru files in real repos (the community comment calls the benefit 'purported' rather than reporting usage).

support.subject: As a developer, I can store collections as plain text files in my repo and version them with git

citations.quote: Bruno stores your collections directly in a folder on your filesystem. We use a plain text markup language, Bru, to save information about API requests.
Collections live as plain text files on your filesystem, so you can version them with Git and review API changes like code.
Run the following command to initialize Git in the Bruno collection directory: git init
Bruno's built-in Git interface — init, diff, pull, commit, and more without leaving the app.
saves API request collection files in simple, human-readable text files that are designed to be committed to a source control repo and easily shared
